title: RDFR-CI: Reference Implementation, Scenario Library and Evaluation Harness
description:
RDFR-CI v1.4.1 is the reproducibility release accompanying the revised study "RDFR-CI: Risk-Driven Deployment and Forensic Readiness for Governing AI Authority in Critical Infrastructure Protection".

The release supports evaluation of the RDFR-CI governance framework, which separates AI detection capability from the authority to execute defensive actions in critical-infrastructure and operational-technology environments. RDFR-CI combines threat exposure, detection capability gap, AI-specific risk, forensic-readiness risk, and cyber-physical consequence with independent safety, availability, forensic-accountability, AI-assurance, and human-authorization constraints.

This version extends the reproducibility material with:

  • robustness analysis under changes to inputs, weights, and authority-band boundaries;
  • evaluation of 24 alternative parameterizations;
  • comparison of policy variants and alternative decision methods;
  • a chronologically held-out labeled-attack evaluation on the public HAI 21.03 industrial-control-system dataset, with removal of the calibration–test overlap and detector-seed sensitivity;
  • a replication of that protocol on HAI 22.04 and HAI 23.05;
  • a second-system evaluation on the BATADAL (C-Town) water-distribution benchmark, under a protocol and predictions fixed before analysis, with its deviation record;
  • a hydraulic simulation of defensive actions on the C-Town network (WNTR) that measures the consequence of incorrect actions and compares policy variants under stated assumptions;
  • a rerun of the SWaT A11 threshold-transfer analysis with training-referenced score normalization and a constructed-event challenge whose specification was fixed before scoring; and
  • scripts that reproduce the manuscript tables and figures, with input-file hashes, library versions, and tests.

The labeled evaluations examine the detector-to-authority component of RDFR-CI and provide evidence for detection-gap and assurance-gate behavior on three releases of one physical testbed (HAI) and on one simulated network (BATADAL). The C-Town simulation examines the consequence dimension and the safety and availability gates in a model, not in an operating plant. These analyses do not constitute operational validation of the governance framework. Validation of threat exposure, AI-specific risk, and forensic readiness, practitioner calibration of the parameters, controlled defensive actions in operating systems, and generalization to further physical testbeds remain future work.

This archive intentionally does not include the manuscript. Raw SWaT data are not redistributed (only derived outputs and input-file hashes are included). The public HAI and BATADAL datasets are referenced rather than copied into the archive.
